original_test_intent: Verify one explicitly selected BMC Journal log entry can be securely retrieved from the correct Manager/LogService parent chain and is schema-valid, readable and semantically correct.
original_method: Discover the exact Manager, Journal LogService and Entries collection, select an owner-approved Entry by immutable @odata.id/event expectation rather than guessing ID, GET it read-only, validate provenance/schema/timestamp/severity/message fields and retain a policy-redacted artifact.
manual_activity: The owner names the intended event/entry and expected field semantics, approves retention/redaction and adjudicates whether the selected entry is correct rather than merely readable.
required_inputs: Exact BMC, Manager, LogService and Entries collection identities
Owner-approved target entry selection rule/ID/event and expected occurrence window
Matching LogEntry schema and required ID, Created, Severity, Message/MessageId and OEM fields
TLS trust, protected read-only credentials and session policy
Sensitive-field redaction and evidence retention rules
safety_requirements: Discover and validate every parent link; never trust an unverified numeric/string Entry ID
Validate TLS and keep credentials out of commands, URLs, output and evidence
Use GET only; prohibit ClearLog, DELETE and any action
Bound payload/traversal and redact sensitive topology/security/fault content under policy
Stop on wrong parent, stale/ambiguous entry, schema/auth/certificate failure or unredactable content
agent_execution_scope: Discover/verify exact parent chain and list candidate entry metadata read-only
Apply the owner selection rule to one exact @odata.id and record why it was chosen
GET and validate status, ResourceType/schema, ID, timestamps, severity and message semantics
Redact/store evidence with parent provenance and report discrepancies for engineer verdict
Perform no log mutation or independent event selection assumption
engineer_actions: Define the intended entry/event, expected field values/time window and parent service
Approve sensitive-data handling and least-privilege access
Review provenance/content evidence and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A Redfish GET of an entry is source-aligned, but unresolved path variables, curl -k/CLI credentials and pretty printing do not verify parent provenance, target-event selection, schema or semantics.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Discover the parent chain, deterministically select the approved entry, retrieve it through verified TLS/protected authentication, validate LogEntry fields and preserve redacted structured evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Manager bmc, Journal service, Entry <Id>, read/correctness goal and 5/5-minute estimates remain as source context; identities are discovered rather than assumed.

modernized_recommendation.status: HIGH PACKAGE-GATED SINGLE LOGENTRY PROVENANCE VALIDATION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Represent selection as parent collection snapshot + selection predicate + chosen @odata.id; hash the redacted response and validate Created/time zone, Severity, MessageId/args and OEM fields against an event oracle.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds deterministic event selection, provenance/schema/semantics and privacy protection instead of fetching an arbitrary ID and pretty-printing it.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Any valid LogEntry JSON does not prove the intended event was read. The chosen entry must match the approved event and time window under the exact Manager/Journal parent chain.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Log entries can rotate between listing and retrieval and contain sensitive data. Stable identity or a bounded snapshot strategy is required; missing/rotated evidence must remain BLOCKED/FAIL for owner review, not prompt mutation.

project_override_considerations: If Journal naming or fields are OEM-specific, the project contract must map them explicitly and retain the source's entry-level readability/correctness objective.
expected_evidence: Exact source row/variant/hash and BMC/Manager/LogService/Entries parent identities
Collection snapshot, owner selection predicate and chosen exact Entry @odata.id
LogEntry schema plus ID/time/severity/message/OEM comparison to expected event
Redaction/retention report, no-log-mutation audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, URI and Criteria consistently target one Journal log entry. The placeholder ID and unspecified correctness/event oracle are execution inputs rather than contradictory source requirements.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Exact entry selection and expected semantics gate DUT execution, but the static review fully records those prerequisites and can proceed.

review_improvement: Turns an arbitrary insecure entry fetch into a provenance-bound event validation with stable selection, semantic fields and privacy controls.
independent_technical_reasoning: Entry correctness depends on provenance and event identity. The same Entry ID can be meaningful only within its Manager/LogService/Entries parent and collection snapshot, and rotating logs can make an ID stale. A deterministic selection rule tied to an expected event/time window is therefore required before GET. Pretty JSON confirms syntax, not that Severity, timestamp or message describe the intended condition, while unrestricted full output can leak exactly the diagnostic information under test.
